Thanks Samantha — this is helpful. A few clarifying Qs before I send a sizing + pricing proposal:
1) Do you expect generation lengths to be uniform (most around 480 tokens) or a heavy tail where ~10% of requests are 1k+ tokens?
2) Are you planning to use prefix/KV cache for repeated system prompts or long histories? That materially reduces KV memory pressure and can lower GPU requirements.
3) Any hard constraints on cold-start latency (e.g., must serve first token within X ms after idle)?

Prelim estimator (very rough):
- If most generations are ~480 tokens and you have sustained peak concurrency ~120, a good starting pool is 6 GPUs (A100-80GB equivalence) configured with continuous batching and prefix cache.
- That setup targets ~p50 latency 200–300ms and p95 ~450–600ms depending on batching window and seq length.
- For 30–60 minute spikes to 200 we recommend a 2-GPU burst capacity (hot standby) or autoscale buffer for predictable spikes.

Ballpark reserved pricing (monthly committed spend, before discounts):
- 6-GPU baseline pool (sustained): $78,000 / month
- +2-GPU burst buffer (on-demand reserve): additional $28,000 / month when used

Standard committed-discount guidance: 12-month commit: ~18–22% off list; 24-month: ~28–33% off list.

I'll draft a precise proposal with performance assumptions once you confirm Q1–Q3. If you'd like, I can include an explicit throughput SLA for business hours with credits for missed p95 targets (requires legal review).
